title: Playlist and Yearbook
premise: Juniper Coldharbour, a scholarship senior at Ashgrove Academy, has survived fifteen years by being invisible — until a college essay prompt ('What is the worst thing you've ever done?') is accidentally published school-wide, and the anonymous confessions that flood back expose a hit-and-run that killed a student two years ago. As Juniper investigates using the yearbook archives and a shared playlist of songs tied to that night, they discover their best friend Theo was in the car — and so, unknowingly, was Juniper's scholarship benefactor. Winning the state debate championship becomes Juniper's only leverage to force a public reckoning before graduation erases everything. In the end, Juniper sacrifices the safe future the scholarship promised to tell the truth on stage, and the academy's powerful family finally faces justice outside its walls.
about_author: O. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former boarding-school teacher who spent a decade watching institutions protect their reputations above their students. They write young adult fiction about kids who refuse to be careful anymore.

chapters.title: The Question Nobody Can Stop Answering
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A glitch publishes the confidential essay prompt to the whole school; anonymous confessions begin appearing on a shared document overnight. Juniper reads them compulsively, recognizing one entry describing a hit-and-run from two years ago. Emotional beat: the thrill of honesty cracking open a world built on performance.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, flashback-woven. We learn how Juniper earned the Coldharbour Scholarship and why invisibility is survival for a kid with no safety net. The confession about the accident keeps pulling them back. Beat: longing to be seen versus terror of it.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair in the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the library archive, Juniper finds the yearbook from two years ago: student Eli Vance, photo printed but no memorial page, as if erased. A librarian warns them off. Beat: first cold proof that someone curated the truth.

chapters.title: Theo Knows Something
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Theo, Juniper's best friend since freshman year, who goes pale when the confession thread surfaces. He lies badly about where he was the night of the accident. Beat: loyalty beginning to strain under weight.

chapters.title: Playlist for a Rainy Night
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Cross-referencing Eli's public playlist with timestamps, Juniper realizes the last song played matches the confession's details — the accident happened near the old quarry road. Beat: grief arriving through music before facts.

chapters.title: The Benefactor's Smile
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At a donor gala, Juniper meets Marcus Whitfield, whose family trust funds the scholarship — and notices Whitfield's son Daniel flinch at Eli's name. Beat: the vertigo of realizing generosity can be hush money.

chapters.title: Debate Season Opens
chapters.summary: Juniper and Theo's POV alternating. Coach announces the state championship could secure Juniper a full ride anywhere. But the season's resolution topic is 'justice versus mercy,' uncomfortably on the nose. Beat: ambition and investigation colliding.

chapters.title: What Theo Confessed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo admits he was in the passenger seat the night Daniel Whitfield's car struck Eli — and that he was paid to stay silent, his own tuition covered ever since. Beat: betrayal and heartbreak; Juniper walks out into the rain.

chapters.title: The Document Gets Deleted
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The confession thread vanishes; the administration calls an assembly about 'digital misconduct.' Someone with power is scrubbing. Juniper saved screenshots. Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Eli's Sister
chapters.summary: New POV: Marisol Vance, who transferred schools after Eli's death and never believed 'he ran off.' Juniper approaches her; she shares Eli's journal, which names D.W. Beat: two investigators becoming allies; righteous anger.

chapters.title: Round One: Win Ugly
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. First tournament; Juniper debates brilliantly while distracted, nearly self-destructs, then channels rage into a devastating rebuttal. Theo watches from the bleachers, not speaking to them. Beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: The Journal's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Eli's final pages describe being followed, threatened after he saw something at the Whitfield estate. The accident may not have been an accident. Beat: dread deepening — this is bigger than one bad night.

chapters.title: Scholarship Review
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Headmaster quietly warns Juniper that 'distractions' endanger their funding — a velvet threat. Juniper realizes the scholarship itself is the leash. Beat: the cost of carelessness made explicit.

chapters.title: Daniel Breaks
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Haunted and drunk at a party, Daniel almost confesses publicly; Theo drags him out. He tells Theo he doesn't remember the impact — only his father's hands on the wheel after. Beat: guilt as a living thing.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Juniper and Marisol's POV. They obtain dashcam audio from the quarry road showing Marcus Whitfield arrived first and moved Eli's body. Now they have evidence — and no legal standing to use it. Beat: triumph curdling into helplessness.

chapters.title: Semifinals: Justice Versus Mercy
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper must argue the side they despise (mercy for the powerful) and wins by making it personal, nearly exposing the case mid-round. The auditorium buzzes. Beat: the mask slipping in public.

chapters.title: Theo Chooses
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo decides to testify despite his family's threats, giving Juniper his signed statement. Reconciliation scene, quiet and bruised. Beat: loyalty realigned with truth.

chapters.title: They Take Everything
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The academy revokes Juniper's scholarship hours before finals; Whitfield lawyers circle Marisol. Juniper has lost the future they spent fifteen years building. Beat: rock bottom — and strange freedom.

chapters.title: Finals: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper competes unfunded, unafraid, and delivers the round of their life — then sets their notes aside during closing statements. Beat: the calm before the detonation.

chapters.title: Closing Statement
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, climax. On stage, live-streamed, Juniper abandons the debate and tells the whole story: Eli, the recording, the cover-up, naming Marcus Whitfield. The room erupts; the stream spreads within minutes. Beat: catharsis — truth spoken where it cannot be deleted.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. State police reopen the case; Whitfield is arrested; the headmaster resigns. Daniel turns himself in. Marisol gets her brother's memorial page. Beat: justice arriving imperfectly, outside the law's original silence.

chapters.title: The Essay I Actually Wrote
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, epilogue. Months later, at a state school on a modest aid package, Juniper submits the honest essay — answering the prompt with their own name attached. Final image: a new playlist, first song shared with Theo and Marisol. Beat: identity chosen, not granted.
